result:
Done. Here's what I did and why.

**Recognized in March: $36,000 (M1 only)**

- **JE-00305** (US, dated 2026-03-14): Dr 2200 Deferred Revenue / Cr 4200 Professional Services Revenue, $36,000. Support attached: SOW (DOC-0047), signed M1 acceptance certificate (DOC-0184), and the 50% advance invoice (DOC-0049).
- Routed for controller approval since it exceeds the $10k posting limit — status is pending.
- US "Revenue recognition" checklist item set to in_progress (it's the revenue accountant's item and covers all US revenue, so I didn't close it).

**Reasoning under ASC 606**

- The SOW carves the $120k fee into three distinct, separately-accepted deliverables — three performance obligations, priced at the contractual 30/50/20 split.
- Control transfers at a point in time on written acceptance. The contract says the customer has no rights to, and no obligation to pay for, a deliverable before acceptance, so acceptance is substantive and none of the over-time criteria are met (no enforceable right to payment for work to date, in particular).
- **M1:** signed off by Evergreen's VP Operations on 2026-03-14 → earned, $36,000.
- **M2:** the PM's 3/27 email puts the build at ~80%, but UAT hasn't started and nothing is signed. Percent-complete is irrelevant under this contract, so $0 — and no contract asset either, since there's no right to consideration yet.
- **M3:** not started, $0.

**Result:** 2200 Deferred Revenue is now $24,000 credit, which ties exactly to the unearned remainder of the $60k non-refundable advance. That $24k releases when M2 is accepted (targeted late April), with the other $36k of M2 billable at that point.

No exceptions flagged — M2 isn't unsupported, it just isn't earned yet. The only open action is the controller's approval of JE-00305.
